roundSummary: The tester's one failure was that GitHub had run nothing on this pull request: it was CONFLICTING against main, so GitHub computed no merge ref and started no workflow run on any of the branch's three commits. This round merges main forward in one commit (793974db), resolves the one conflict, follows the one sentence the base made stale, and leaves the pull request MERGEABLE, so the run the tester needs now exists. No code of the change itself was altered.

proof.criterion: The tester's failure: on this pull request's own runs the docs race job's conclusion and the remaining lane can be read at all. GitHub started no run because the pull request was CONFLICTING.
proof.surface: The pull request on GitHub: its mergeability, which decides whether GitHub computes a merge ref and starts the router's workflow.
proof.command: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && base=$(gh pr view 2516 -R sjawhar/legion --json baseRefName -q '.baseRefName | @json') && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git fetch && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" new legion/INFRA-756 "${base}@origin" -m 'merge: resolve conflict against main@origin' ; then resolve packages/envoy/AGENTS.md, push the bookmark, and read: gh pr view 2516 --repo sjawhar/legion --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus,headRefOid

After the merge and push: {"headRefOid":"793974db91a695c276c70be58a344297199fcc66","mergeStateStatus":"BLOCKED","mergeable":"MERGEABLE"} — BLOCKED is the base's own required-review and required-check state, not a conflict, so GitHub now computes the merge ref and runs the router.

The conflict was real, not mechanical — both sides rewrote the same Critical conventions bullet to a different six-job list — so an automatic union would have dropped one job's name.

filesChanged: packages/envoy/AGENTS.md: the Critical conventions bullet is the union of both sides — seven Envoy jobs, dispatch-memory, dispatch-multiprocess, listener-server-change, broker-multiprocess, envoy-go-race, envoy-go-race-docs and envoy-infra-go. This was the merge's one conflict.

.github/workflows/ci.yaml: the go-envoy cache paragraph, which this pull request already rewrote, names listener-server-change, the base's new job, which restores and saves that family. Everything else of this pull request's ci.yaml diff is unchanged.
Unchanged by this round: .github/scripts/ci_job_reads.py and docs/testing.md merged clean and their lines are the same.
trickyParts: The merge is one commit made with `jj new legion/INFRA-756 main@origin`, never a rebase: the branch is in a clone every issue workspace shares, where a rebase would rewrite every descendant of the fork point, another tree's stacked branch included. The merge descends from both the bookmark's old position and main, so the push is a genuine fast-forward and carries no skip-checks line.

The forward-merge fingerprint changed (8f6dc4b8… → fb046c63…), so this head goes through the tester again rather than counting as a confirmation. Two files of the pull request's own diff moved: AGENTS.md (the conflict) and ci.yaml (the one stale sentence). The comment on the pull request names both.
The drift check now reports 25 gates, not 24: the base added listener-server-change. A reader comparing this round's output with the first round's should expect that difference and no other.
deviations: The measured time and both jobs' conclusions remain the tester's to read on CI, as the plan's acceptance table assigns them; an implementer never waits on this pull request's CI. The first round could not be judged on that point at all, since GitHub had started no run; it now has a mergeable head to run.
discoveredComplexity: A pull request GitHub reports CONFLICTING gets no merge ref and therefore no workflow run at all — not a red run, no run — so a tester reading `gh pr checks` sees 'no checks reported on the branch' and can judge nothing. The first round's implementer pushed and completed without reading that state. Reading `gh pr view <n> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` right after the push is the cheap check that catches it, and it needs no wait on CI.

The base's new listener-server-change job joined the go-envoy cache family in the same window, which made one sentence of the paragraph this pull request rewrote wrong at the merge. A forward merge can leave prose stale in a file that merged clean; the enumerating sentences of ci.yaml's header are where that shows.
